title: Five stages, five proofs
spec: Capstone · the pipeline end to end
intro: A map of the build, not a tutorial. One stage per step: the artifact it produces, and the check that proves the artifact is real. The lab packet has the eighteen steps; this is the shape they add up to.

provenance.source: a walk of labs/CAPSTONE-knowledge-pipeline/README.md over labs/sample-project; every command and output is taken from the lab solutions, cited per step

foot: Build it for real: labs/CAPSTONE-knowledge-pipeline/README.md — seven phases, eighteen steps, two deliberate sabotages.

steps.title: Stage 1 — extract the structural graph
narrative: The structural layer is deterministic extraction: identical source in, identical graph out, zero LLM calls and therefore zero hallucination risk on extracted edges. That is what lets the provenance tag on an edge honestly say EXTRACTED.

Artifact: graphify-out/graph.json. Check: orderflow is small enough to verify by hand — that is why the course uses it. Every ground-truth relationship listed in sample-project/README.md must appear, and an in-degree tally must put the shared/ modules at the top: that cluster is the god node the architecture doc warned about, and its centrality is what makes a change there a wide-blast-radius change.
steps.youDo: graphify update . if it is installed, or the offline fallback: python ../shared_tools/kg_extract.py . --out graphify-out/graph.json

terminal.text: python -c "…Counter over graph['edges']…"   # in-degree by module

steps.title: Stage 2 — author the OKF bundle
narrative: The graph knows what the code is. It cannot know that WAU excludes testers on purpose, or that ADR-001 chose an in-process bus over a broker. That intent is the narrative layer: three Service concepts, two analytics concepts, an index.md the agent reads pre-flight, and a log.md recording what the bundle knows changed.

Artifact: knowledge/. Check: lint returns zero errors, and the WAU concept is an attested computation — it names services/orders/metrics.py::weekly_active_users as the source of truth rather than restating the rule in prose that can drift away from the code.
steps.youDo: python ../M06-okf-authoring/solution/validate.py knowledge — and keep the body structure identical across Service concepts, because consistency is what agents parse.

steps.title: Stage 3 — install the enrichment hook
narrative: A bundle nobody maintains is a wiki nobody reads. The post-commit hook scopes its scan to the git diff — touch webhooks.py and only billing-service.md is rescanned. Diff-scoping is the entire cost model: full-repo rescans per commit are what make teams switch pipelines off.

Artifact: .git/hooks/post-commit. Check: two behaviours, not one. A real change refreshes exactly one concept and appends log.md; a broken concept makes the hook fail loudly, non-zero. Note what this hook deliberately does not have: no nohup, no backgrounding, no silent resource-gated skips — the three mechanisms M11 catalogued.
steps.youDo: Sabotage #1: delete the type: line from a concept, commit any code change, and confirm the hook exits non-zero naming the file. Then restore it.

steps.title: Stage 4 — serve both layers over MCP
narrative: Two artifacts on disk help nobody until an agent can reach them in one round trip. The MCP server exposes graph_callers, graph_callees and the composite explore over stdio, and index.md routes canonical questions to the right concept file.

Artifact: a registered server. Check: --selftest before you trust anything — a silently broken server plus graceful fallback produces confident garbage that looks like a successful run. Then the three baseline questions come back in one tool call each, and an unknown symbol returns an honest miss instead of a plausible guess.
steps.youDo: python server.py --selftest must print SELFTEST PASSED before you run claude mcp add orderflow-graph -- python /abs/path/to/server.py.

steps.title: Stage 5 — wire the CI freshness gate
narrative: Every stage so far works on the day you built it. The gate is about every day after. It compares graph.json's mtime against git log -1 --format=%ct, cross-checks stored node and edge counts against a fresh extraction, and blocks — exit 1 — before any pipeline step that would trust the map.

Artifacts: ci/freshness_gate.py and a four-line ci/ci.sh that runs the gate and the bundle lint under set -e. Check: green on a healthy repo, then sabotage #2 — commit with --no-verify so the hook never fires — and watch it exit 1 with an actionable message.
Read the last line of that message. It names the MCP restart, because regeneration alone does not fix a running server that loaded the old graph at startup and has no hot-reload.
steps.youDo: Sabotage #2: git commit --allow-empty -qm "commit without rebuilding the graph" --no-verify, then run the gate.

CROSS-CHECK OK: stored counts match a fresh extraction

STALE: graph.json predates HEAD by 1 commit(s)

steps.title: What you can honestly claim at the end
narrative: Phase 7 is the part most builds skip. Divide your Phase-1 token counts by Phase-5's and expect a single-digit multiple — then write down in NOTES.md why that is the correct result rather than a disappointment. orderflow is roughly fifteen files, far below the ~500-file floor where graph tooling pays for itself; the exploration a graph eliminates barely exists at this scale.

The comparison is the lesson. The 71.5× headline was a ceiling case on a favourable 52-file corpus; independent replications landed at 6.8×–49×, and 7.3× on a from-scratch Python codebase. Savings scale with the size of the haystack — VS Code's 10,000 files saved 78%, OkHttp's 645 files saved 13%. Your small number on a tiny repo is benchmark literacy acquired first-hand.

And then the one question that decides whether any of this is production: how would I detect a stale graph within 24 hours? Name the script, what it compares, where it runs, what it does on failure, and the MCP restart. If you can write that paragraph about your own system, it is airworthy. If you cannot, it is a demo that has not failed yet.
steps.youDo: Write both paragraphs in NOTES.md — the honest multiple, and the mechanical staleness answer — before you call the capstone done.
